government.note: Parliamentary republic with symmetric bicameralism: the government must hold the confidence of both the Chamber of Deputies and the Senate. The President of the Republic is elected for seven years by Parliament in joint session plus 58 regional delegates, appoints the Prime Minister, and can dissolve Parliament; when the President is unable to act, the President of the Senate acts (Art. 86).

system.note: In 2000 the 1993 Mattarella law (Mattarellum) applied: 75% of seats by first-past-the-post, 25% by proportional representation with a 4% threshold and the scorporo compensation mechanism (used 1994, 1996, 2001). The 2005 law (Porcellum) introduced closed-list PR with a majority bonus of at least 340 seats for the winning coalition (used 2006, 2008, 2013). The 2017 law (Rosatellum) is a mixed system with a 3% list threshold (used 2018, 2022). The 2020 constitutional referendum cut the Chamber from 630 to 400 seats from the 2022 election (147 FPTP, 245 PR, 8 abroad). seats_2000 is the 1996 election result.

system.note: 315 elected senators plus senators for life (former Presidents ex officio and presidential appointees). Under the 1993 law, 75% of seats were elected in single-member constituencies and 25% by a regional proportional method among losing candidates; from 2006 regional closed-list PR with regional majority bonuses (Porcellum); from 2018 the mixed Rosatellum. The 2020 constitutional referendum cut the elected Senate from 315 to 200 from the 2022 election (74 FPTP, 122 PR, 4 abroad). seats_2000 is the 1996 result plus 9 senators for life.
